name: Salta
summary_text: The national dossier found no province-specific trans statute, enforcement series or incident pattern for Salta; it is among the units classified "no sub-national signal", with the caveat that such provinces retain the contravención/faltas police codes documented as the instrument of most arrests of trans and travesti people, and that northern interior provinces have neither a visible community presence nor reporting infrastructure to generate records — so the absence of documentation is not demonstrated safety. The February 2025 national decrees curtailing the Gender Identity Law (minors' transition treatments; prison placement of trans detainees) apply to Salta as to all provinces, within a deteriorating national picture (a record 227 anti-LGBT hate crimes in 2025, up 62%).

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (absent from the article cache); the underlying source is an April 2025 Washington Blade feature reporting that Argentina's transgender community faces a "chaotic, desperate situation" amid the national government's policies toward the LGBTI+ community.

sources.title: Crímenes de odio en Argentina: aumento y récord de uno cada 38 horas - Agencia Presentes
sources.claim_summary: Agencia Presentes report (19 March 2026) on the Observatorio Nacional de Crímenes de Odio's 2025 tally: at least 227 hate crimes against people for sexual orientation or gender identity, up 62% year-on-year and the record of the observatory's ten years of operation — one every 38 hours; perpetrators were predominantly security-force personnel and unidentified attackers in public space, beating the main modality, in a context the observatory attributes to the national government's "cultural battle" against LGBTI+ people; attacks continued in early 2026, including a life-endangering home invasion of an LGBTIQ+ organisation president in Jujuy.
